items.sentence1: We will go ahead with the outdoor concert unless the forecast changes.
items.before: We will go ahead with the outdoor concert
fullAnswers: provided that the forecast does not

explanation.en: Part 1: 'provided (that) the forecast' replaces 'unless' and means 'only if'. Part 2: because 'unless' already contains a negative, the new clause needs 'does not change'.
explanation.cs: Část 1: provided (that) = pokud, za podmínky že. Část 2: unless v sobě nese zápor (pokud ne), takže po provided musíme zápor doplnit: does not / doesn't change.

items.sentence1: 'You broke the printer on purpose, Tom!' said Kate.

explanation.en: Part 1: the pattern is 'accuse somebody of', so Tom must follow the verb. Part 2: a preposition is followed by the -ing form, 'breaking' or 'having broken'.
explanation.cs: Část 1: vazba accuse somebody of (obvinit koho z čeho). Část 2: po předložce of následuje -ing tvar: breaking nebo having broken.

items.sentence1: It is believed that the thieves escaped through a back window.
fullAnswers: are believed to have got away
are believed to have got out

explanation.en: Part 1: the personal passive starts with the subject, 'The thieves are believed'. Part 2: the escape happened before the believing, so the perfect infinitive 'to have escaped' is needed.
explanation.cs: Část 1: osobní pasivum: The thieves are believed. Část 2: útěk proběhl dřív než 'věří se', proto infinitiv minulý: to have escaped.

items.sentence1: I'm sure Mark didn't see the message, or he would have replied.
items.after: the message, or he would have replied.

explanation.en: Part 1: 'I'm sure ... didn't' is a negative deduction, expressed with 'can't' or 'couldn't'. Part 2: the deduction is about the past, so 'have seen' follows the modal. 'Mustn't have' is avoided here, as it is not the standard British form for deduction.
explanation.cs: Část 1: jistota, že se něco nestalo = can't / couldn't. Část 2: jde o minulost, proto have + příčestí: have seen. Mustn't have v britské angličtině pro dedukci běžně nepoužíváme.

items.sentence1: Paul didn't realise that the job would be so difficult.

explanation.en: Part 1: 'didn't realise' becomes the fixed phrase 'had no idea'. Part 2: 'so difficult' becomes an indirect question, 'how difficult the job would be'. 'How hard' and 'how tough' are accepted too.
explanation.cs: Část 1: ustálené spojení have no idea = vůbec netušit. Část 2: 'so difficult' se mění na nepřímou otázku how difficult (s oznamovacím slovosledem the job would be). Uznává se i how hard nebo how tough.

items.sentence1: The sequel was much less entertaining than the original film.
fullAnswers: not anywhere near as entertaining as

explanation.en: Part 1: 'much less' becomes 'nowhere near', a strong negative comparison. Part 2: it is followed by the equative 'as entertaining as'. 'Nearly' would change the key word.
explanation.cs: Část 1: nowhere near = zdaleka ne (silnější než 'not as'). Část 2: srovnání as + přídavné jméno + as. Nearly nelze, klíčové slovo se nesmí měnit.
